newsitem.title: UK: Johnston Press says outlook encouraging.
newsitem.headline: Johnston Press says outlook encouraging.

text.p: Johnston Press Plc, one of Britain's leading regional newspaper groups, said on Wednesday that trading conditions had improved for its core business and that the outlook was encouraging.
"Trading conditions in the local and regional newspaper industry have improved in the last six months," chairman Fred Johnston said in a statement.

"Both advertising volumes and revenues are currently more encouraging in many areas and reflect the stronger performance of the national economy...On the whole the outlook is encouraging, particularly for the company's newspapers."
Johnston added that an election year always brought an element of uncertainty but added "there are no apparent signs of storms on the horizon".
The company earlier reported a 43 percent rise in 1996 pre-tax profit to 24.1 million stg on turnover of 165 million, up 61 percent.
The profits were boosted by a six month contribution from the regional newspapers which Johnston bought from media group EMAP Plc last year.
The 213 million stg acquisition was the largest expansion in Johnston's history.
Johnston said further profit growth should be attainable in the newspaper division, particularly as the company has yet to reap the full benefits of the integration of its recent buys.
"There remains much to do in 1997 with progress anticipated on both the cost and the revenue side resulting in better prospects than there have been for some time," the chairman said.
The company said newspaper advertising revenues were six percent ahead of the previous year, on a like for like basis.
